A Flask application is configured with a static folder path that ends with a forward slash (e.g., 'frontend/build/'). The application also defines a custom catch-all route using @app.route('/<path:path>') that should handle any URL path not matched by other routes.

Currently, when a client requests a path that is not a real static file (for example '/some/custom/path'), instead of the catch-all route handling the request, the static file endpoint intercepts the request and returns a 404.

Expected behavior: When a request path does not correspond to an actual static file, the custom catch-all route should handle the request, not the static endpoint.

Fix the routing so that the static endpoint only matches paths that correspond to actual files in the static folder, and all other paths fall through to the catch-all route.

from flask import Flask
import os
os.makedirs('frontend/build', exist_ok=True)
app = Flask(__name__, static_folder='frontend/build/')
@app.route('/<path:path>')
def catch_all(path):
    return 'catch-all-ok'
with app.test_client() as c:
    r = c.get('/some/custom/path')
    assert r.status_code == 200, f'Expected 200, got {r.status_code}'
    assert r.data == b'catch-all-ok', f'Expected catch-all-ok, got {r.data}'
    print('PASS')
"
